text.p: French tobacco maker Seita said on Thursday that it renewed its licensing agreements with the major cigarette, cigar, pipe and rolling tobacco manufacturers for which it handles product distribution in France.

It said 30 manufacturers, including B.A.T, Imperial Tobacco and Philip Morris had "entrusted the delivery of the tobacco products they market in France to Seita" under the deals, which run for three years.
Seita said that, since 1977, tobacco product distribution has been carried out via negotiated commercial agreements. Before then, it had a legal monopoly on wholesale distribution.
Supplying France's 35,000 tobacconists is Seita's second most important activity. In 1995, the group posted revenues of 10.7 billion francs from this activity.
